newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIA OTC STOCKS RECOVER FROM SELLING PRESURE.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIA OTC STOCKS RECOVER FROM SELLING PRESURE.

text.p: Romania's over-the-counter market (OTC) stocks closed up on Wednesday, recovering after a downmove at mid-day under strong selling pressure in some high-caps listings, traders said.
They said the mid-day downswing was triggered by big players' attempts to create anxiety among small investors and force them to jump into the market with selling orders.
"Wednesday's step back is a technique of big investors to move the market and force the scared small investors to sell before prices would go lower," one operator said.
Big investors then engulf the stocks thrown out on the market by small players, he added.
Traders forecast a slight recovery on Thursday, which would be more certain on Friday.
Gainers outnumbered losers by 137 to 100 at Wednesday's session, when 324 stocks remained flat.

Unofficial indices VAB-RA, computed by Vanguard securities, and BIG-OTC, compiled by the BIG brokerage house, fell to 3,430.4 and 2,466.52 points respectively, a decline of 2.7 percent and 4.15 percent. Those indices are computed based on average prices of OTC listings.
Operators said two cement makers plus steel mill Sidex, all of which have an important weight on the indices, saw average prices down but recovered in late trading.
Sidex's average price tumbled 15.7 percent, but the stock closed 500 lei stronger at 13,500, against 13,000 on Tuesday.
Cement maker Moldocim also lost 14.2 percent on average price but ended flat at 28,500 lei from the previous session.
Oil refinery Arpechim firmed 100 lei to 25,600, while Petromidia, another oil refinery, gained 1,000 lei to 17,500.
Overall market turnover fell to 7.3 billion lei from 9.5 billion on Tuesday, with three million shares changing hands.
